title: Closing thoughts and Columbia jam session records
summary: He is happy to have worked with so many players and praises his Columbia jam session records.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Well now, time is running out. Have you any last minute observations to make on your life or on, I mean....
Well, I'm just happy that I've been on the scene for the length of time and I'm more than happy to have worked with so many
Well I was always very happy that we made that record you know with Coleman Hawkins.
You know that was nothing to do with me in a sense, but it was just a piece of luck that that came off as well as it did.
Right. Yes, I enjoyed that day too. I enjoyed that day, very much.

But there's one thing about it, I mean you have, you have been recorded; you know we've never mentioned some of the records that I think people still consider classics of the kind. Of their kind, you know those jam session records you made for Columbia.
They were great things that, some of them, most of the early ones we made.
know to my mind they were much better than the sort of Jazz the Philharmonic jam sessions because there was a certain integrity of style there. You hadn't got, they were not exhibitionistic.
No, no. I tell you I liked them. They were pretty popular in Europe, too.
The 'Huckle buck' and all those things. And we had some very good guys on those dates. Very nice guys.
That kind of record can still be made you know. But I don't know how long.
